zh.principle: **协议**：DTLS 1.3（DTLS 1.3）。摘要给出范围与继承：「This document specifies version 1.3 of the Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) protocol.DTLS 1.3 allows client/server applications to communicate over the Internet in a way that is designed to prevent eavesdropping, tampering, and message forgery.」
zh.why: 继承关系与安全例外写在同一段：「The DTLS 1.3 protocol is based on the Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.3 protocol and provides equivalent security guarantees with the exception of order protection / non-replayability.」§3 说明必须改记录层的第一个理由：「TLS relies on an implicit sequence number on records.」序号错位会让后续记录解密失败，因此「DTLS solves this problem by adding sequence numbers to records.」
zh.used: §5 表明复用策略：DTLS 1.3 沿用 TLS 1.3 的握手消息与流程，并「reuses TLS 1.3's “cookie” extension to provide a return-routability check as part of connection establishment.」记录层则自成一格：「The DTLS 1.3 record layer is different from the TLS 1.3 record layer and also different from the DTLS 1.2 record layer.」
zh.broken: 放大风险与握手消息弃用构成边界：§5.1 指出「Servers which process 0-RTT requests and send 0.5-RTT responses without a cookie exchange risk being used in an amplification attack if the size of outgoing messages greatly exceeds the size of those that are received.」并给出「A server SHOULD limit the amount of data it sends toward a client address to three times the amount of data sent by the client before it verifies that the client is able to receive data at that address.」§5.2 另规定「DTLS 1.3-compliant implementations MUST NOT use the HelloVerifyRequest to execute a return-routability check.」
zh.history:
RFC 9147 头部为 E.Rescorla（Mozilla）、H.Tschofenig（Arm Limited）与 N.Modadugu（Google, Inc.），类别 Standards Track，2022 年 4 月，标注「Obsoletes: 6347」，没有 Updates 行；§1 简洁说明本文以 TLS 1.3 为基准的增量写法，并写明「It obsoletes DTLS 1.2.」

en.principle: **Protocol**: DTLS 1.3 (DTLS 1.3). The abstract gives scope and lineage: "This document specifies version 1.3 of the Datagram Transport Layer Security (DTLS) protocol. DTLS 1.3 allows client/server applications to communicate over the Internet in a way that is designed to prevent eavesdropping, tampering, and message forgery."
en.why: The same abstract paragraph gives both the lineage and its exception: "The DTLS 1.3 protocol is based on the Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.3 protocol and provides equivalent security guarantees with the exception of order protection / non-replayability." Section 3 names the first reason the record layer must change: "TLS relies on an implicit sequence number on records." — a lost record breaks later decryption — so "DTLS solves this problem by adding sequence numbers to records."
en.used: Section 5 states the reuse strategy: DTLS 1.3 keeps the TLS 1.3 handshake messages and flows and "reuses TLS 1.3's “cookie” extension to provide a return-routability check as part of connection establishment." The record layer is its own design: "The DTLS 1.3 record layer is different from the TLS 1.3 record layer and also different from the DTLS 1.2 record layer."
en.broken: Amplification risk and message deprecation form the boundary: §5.1 warns "Servers which process 0-RTT requests and send 0.5-RTT responses without a cookie exchange risk being used in an amplification attack if the size of outgoing messages greatly exceeds the size of those that are received." and sets "A server SHOULD limit the amount of data it sends toward a client address to three times the amount of data sent by the client before it verifies that the client is able to receive data at that address." Section 5.2 adds that "DTLS 1.3-compliant implementations MUST NOT use the HelloVerifyRequest to execute a return-routability check."
en.history: The RFC 9147 header lists E. Rescorla (Mozilla), H. Tschofenig (Arm Limited) and N. Modadugu (Google, Inc.), Category: Standards Track, April 2022, marked “Obsoletes: 6347” with no Updates line; §1 describes the delta-on-TLS 1.3 presentation and states "It obsoletes DTLS 1.2."

zh: 基于 TLS 1.3：语义与密码学设计直接继承。
顺序保护与非重放：与 TLS 1.3 的唯一安全差异。
epoch 与序号：记录层为数据报补上的状态。
cookie 扩展：沿用 TLS 1.3 的可达性验证。
0.5-RTT：未做 cookie 时的放大风险。
en: Built on TLS 1.3: the semantics and cryptographic design are inherited.
Order protection and non-replayability: the one stated security difference.
Epoch and sequence number: the record-layer state datagrams need.
Cookie extension: TLS 1.3 reachability check reused.
0.5-RTT: the amplification risk when no cookie exchange occurs.
